First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

$$
(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)^{′}=-{csch}^{2}⁡x
$$

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\operatorname{coth}⁡x-\operatorname{csch}⁡x) \\  & =4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{csch}⁡x) \\  & =4(-{csch}^{2}⁡x)-(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =-4{csch}^{2}⁡x+\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x \\  & =\operatorname{csch}⁡x(-4\operatorname{csch}⁡x+\operatorname{coth}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$
